description: Write new Go surface as a ladder: read the package, add the struct, settle its fields, stub the functions, pseudocode the bodies, then fill them and pass the style gate.
systemPrompt: You are writing Go inside a fixed process. You do not choose the order of work: each step tells you exactly what to do, gives you only the tools that step needs, and ends when you call `advance` with one of its options. Do only what the current step asks, even when you can already see the next step's work. When a step asks why, answer concretely about this code, not in generalities. Every exported identifier carries a godoc comment starting with its name. No package-level mutable state.

edges.description: You know the package, its existing types, and its conventions.

nodes.prompt:
Step 2: add exactly one struct for the objective, in its own file, with a godoc comment on the type. Declare the struct with no fields yet, or with only the fields you are certain of. Do not add methods, constructors, or bodies: later steps own those.

Objective: {{task}}
nodes.why: Why does this struct need to exist, what does it own that no existing type owns, and why is this the right file for it?

edges.description: The struct type exists with its godoc comment.

nodes.why: Why is each field required, and why is this set complete rather than one field larger or smaller?

edges.description: You changed the field set and want to judge it again.

nodes.prompt:
Step 4: add the function and method stubs this type needs, each with its godoc comment and its final signature, and each body containing only `panic("not implemented")`. Include the constructor. Write no logic.

Objective: {{task}}
nodes.why: Why is this the right function set and these the right signatures, and what did you deliberately leave out?

edges.description: Every stub compiles with its godoc comment and final signature.

nodes.prompt:
Step 5: replace each stub body with the plan for that body, written as ordinary Go line comments, one comment line per step the body will take, keeping the `panic("not implemented")` beneath them. Design here: this is the last step where changing your mind costs a sentence.

Objective: {{task}}
nodes.why: For each body, why does it take these steps in this order, and where can it fail?

edges.description: Every body carries its plan as comments.

nodes.why: Which body did each edit implement, and where did the implementation depart from its plan?

edges.description: Every stub is implemented and the package builds.
Implementation showed a second type is required.

nodes.prompt: Step 7: the deterministic gate. Run the build, re-read every file you wrote, and fix anything that fails `gofmt` or `go vet`, that leaves an exported identifier without a godoc comment starting with its name, or that introduces package-level mutable state. You cannot leave this step until the gate passes.
nodes.why: What did the gate catch, and which step of the ladder should have caught it instead?

edges.description: The gate passes and the code is finished.
